meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
Write them down yourself, Hale. The zero comes off, I get an apology for how Owen found out, and nothing goes near his record. Now, who decided?
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not drafting your paperwork, Hale; put it in an email yourself. The zero withdrawn, an apology, and Owen's record left untouched. Did anyone speak to Owen before that mark went in?
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
You've asked three times now, Hale, and the answer hasn't changed. You heard my terms. Is anything on Owen's record right now, yes or no?
Use bold for the most important one.
The one that matters most is his record, and it never moves. You still haven't answered me, Hale. I'm writing that down.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
You called this meeting, Hale, so you tell me what you have. If it's a number from a machine, save us both the time. What else is there?
